analysis:
Examined EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (head 1-538 and base 544-953) and the visible patch hunks. Changes: (1) a new catch for MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError.unsupportedOutputControl in the non-throwing submitTokenized overload, which emits a content-free marker error; (2) a new early refusal (head lines ~154-158) calling nativeOutputControlRefusal before duplicate-ID checks, service admission, cache receipt minting, SSD staging or KV reservation; (3) a new helper nativeOutputControlRefusal appended around lines 964-994, whose body is truncated in the patch excerpt and not visible.

Security review: the early refusal sits before any resource acquisition (service allowance, pendingSubmissionIDs, prefix receipts, SSD staging, shared KV, glm5NextGateReservations), so no cleanup path is skipped. It calls usageSignal?.finalizeLookup and then finishes the continuation. The finish before throw matches the existing pattern for advertisedContextExceeded. It narrows what can be admitted, and it converts an untyped 500 into a typed client error. That reduces the availability risk of one client's malformed request striking the coordinator inference-error breaker (relevant to T-010-style availability concerns). I found no new exposure of A-001 prompt data, since the marker is a fixed string supplied by the refusal helper. I could not verify that the refusal string excludes prompt-derived content because the helper body is truncated. Cache scope, TTL and HMAC paths relevant to T-041 (cacheScope, checkpointScope, receipt registration and discard defers) are unchanged. The base 544-953 text is an unchanged tail with respect to changed ranges; the pump, retirement transfer and prefill receipt ownership logic is untouched.

Open questions for integration: confirm the nativeOutputControlRefusal body (head ~964-994) returns only fixed content-free messages and does not throw or mutate state, and that callers of the throwing overload map unsupportedOutputControl to a 400 rather than leaking it as an internal error. I did not see those callers.
